# gulp-build

A common Gulp configuration that can be used to build minified CSS and
Javascript from SASS, CSS and Javascript source files. Also provides
shareable ESLint and Stylelint configurations so linting rules stay
consistent — and only need updating in one place — across every
project that uses this package.

[[_TOC_]]

## Prerequisites

* nodejs version 22 or higher. Node 24 (Active LTS) is the safe
  default; Node 26 also works and is fine to use even though it
  won't become LTS until October 2026 — this is a build-tooling
  dependency, not a production runtime, so riding Current here is
  low-risk. This floor moved up from 16 as of v2.0.0 — Gulp 5,
  ESLint 9's flat config support, and several other modernized
  dependencies all raised it. As of mid-2026, Node 20 has also
  reached end-of-life upstream, so 22 (Maintenance LTS) or higher are
  the only realistic choices regardless. See [Changelog](#changelog).
* access to the gulp-build registry (see below)

## Preinstallation setup: Access to the gulp-build registry

Gulp-build is packaged and stored in the Library's Gitlab registry
under the scope `@dltg` and named `@dltg/gulp-build`.  Complete
details on using the Gitlab registry are found
[here](https://docs.gitlab.com/ee/user/packages/npm_registry/).  Here
is a summary specific to this project.  You will require a personal
access token with scope `api`.  Also note the project ID for
dltg/gulp-build is 432 as found on the project's home page in Gitlab.

1. Set the npm registry configuration:

   ```sh
   npm config set @dltg:registry \
     https://gitlab.library.dartmouth.edu/api/v4/projects/432/packages/npm/
   ```

2. Add your access token to enable access to the registry via the API:
  
   ```sh
   npm config set -- \
     '//gitlab.library.dartmouth.edu/api/v4/projects/432/packages/npm/:_authToken' \
     "<your_token>"`
   ```

(Note: This configuration is saved privately in ~/.npmrc, and may be
edited there if needed, for example, to update the authToken.)

## Installation

To install the package in a new working directory of a project that
already contains gulp-build, run `npm install`.

## Adding to a project

1. Configure registry access (see above).

2. Add gulp-build to the project's package list: `npm add @dltg/gulp-build`.

   Also add `gulp` itself as a direct devDependency of the project:
   `npm add -D gulp`. Gulp's CLI resolves the local `gulp` install
   starting from the project's own `node_modules`, not gulp-build's,
   so this needs to be explicit rather than relying on npm's hoisting
   to surface it. (`gulp-build` declares `gulp` as a peer dependency
   for the same reason — npm will warn if the versions drift apart.)

3. Create a gulpfile.js for the project.  A minimal gulpfile.js which
   reads configuration from `gulp-config.js` and exports all the
   methods defined by gulp-build is shown below.

   ```javascript
   const $conf = require('./gulp-config.js');
   const $build = require('@dltg/gulp-build')($conf);

   module.exports = $build;
   ```

4. Configure gulp-build.  This is typically done with a gulp-config.js
   file as described below.

5. Add an `eslint.config.js` and `.stylelintrc.js` to the root of
   your project, each doing a real `require()` of the shared config
   gulp-build exports. As of v2.0.0 these are live subpath exports of
   the package rather than static template files, so there's nothing
   to symlink or keep in sync by hand — every project simply requires
   the same config.

   `eslint.config.js`:

   ```javascript
   module.exports = require('@dltg/gulp-build/eslint-config');
   ```

   `.stylelintrc.js` (note: **must be `.js`, not `.stylelintrc.json`**
   — see callout below):

   ```javascript
   module.exports = require('@dltg/gulp-build/stylelint-config');
   ```

   A project that needs its own additional rules on top of the shared
   base can layer them rather than forking the whole config:

   ```javascript
   // eslint.config.js
   const base = require('@dltg/gulp-build/eslint-config');
   module.exports = [...base, { rules: { /* project-specific overrides */ } }];
   ```

   ```javascript
   // .stylelintrc.js
   const base = require('@dltg/gulp-build/stylelint-config');
   module.exports = { ...base, rules: { ...base.rules, /* project-specific overrides */ } };
   ```

   > **Why `.stylelintrc.js` and not a `.stylelintrc.json` with
   > `"extends": "@dltg/gulp-build/stylelint-config"`?** They look
   > equivalent but aren't. `eslint.config.js` works with a plain
   > `require()` call because that's real JS executed by Node, which
   > correctly understands this package's `exports` map. A JSON
   > file's `"extends"` field is just a string that *stylelint's own*
   > internal resolver interprets — and that resolver isn't reliably
   > aware of `exports`-map subpaths for scoped packages (it was
   > designed around shareable configs being their own separate
   > packages resolved via a plain `main` field, like
   > `stylelint-config-standard`). In practice this surfaces as
   > `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading
   > 'ignoreFiles')` — stylelint's resolver silently got back nothing.
   > A `.js` config file sidesteps the problem entirely by making the
   > `require()` real.

   > **Migrating an existing project from v1?** Delete any symlinked
   > or copied `.eslintrc.json`/`.stylelintrc.json` (and the
   > `templates/` directory reference) and replace them with the two
   > files above — `eslint.config.js` and `.stylelintrc.js`. ESLint 9
   > requires the flat `eslint.config.js` format — a legacy
   > `.eslintrc.json` will no longer be picked up.

## Tasks

To run any gulp task, use `npx gulp <task>`.  Available tasks can be
listed by running `npx gulp --tasks`.  The tasks are described below.

* **clean** -- remove all Gulp build products.

* **build** -- lint and process all SASS, CSS and Javascript source files
  and update the source file checksums.  Equivalent to performing in
  order: clean, sass, js, cat, and minify and then updating the
  source checksums.

  ```mermaid
  graph TD;
    A[clean] --> B(sass);
    A --> C(js);
    A --> D(cat);
    A --> E(update source checksums);
    
    B --> F(minify);
    C --> F;
    D --> F;
    E --> F;
  ```

* **ubuild** -- lint and process all SASS, CSS and Javascript source
  files and update the source file checksums without
  minification. Equivalent to performing in order: clean, sass, js,
  cat and then updating the source checksums.

* **default** -- an alias for "build", executed by running `npx gulp`
  with no specific task given.
  
* **watch** -- monitor source files and rebuild products if they
  change.  Reload the browserSync URL after rebuilding.
  
* **cat** -- perform the CSS concatenation steps

* **sass** -- lint and compile the SASS files to produce CSS sources

* **jsLint** -- lint the Javascript sources

* **js** -- minify the Javascript sources (via [Terser](https://terser.org/))

* **gulpJsLint** -- lint the Gulp configuration and Javascript files.

* **minify** -- minify the CSS sources

  > **v2.0.0:** The **composerJsonLint** task (linting a project's
  > `composer.json` through the JS linter) has been removed. It
  > relied on running ESLint over a JSON file, which isn't a
  > standard ESLint use case and didn't survive the move to ESLint's
  > flat config / Node API. If any project actually depends on this
  > task, open an issue — it can be reinstated properly (e.g. with
  > `eslint-plugin-jsonc`) rather than carried over as-is.

## Configuring

Configuration for gulp-build is passed to the module during
initialization as properties of an object.  Typically the object is
defined in a gulp-config.js file and loaded by a project's gulpfile.js
prior to loading gulp-build.  A basic gulp-config.js with an empty
configuration looks like this:

```javascript
module.exports = {};
```

The top level of the configuration contains 5 major sections:

* browserSync
* gulp
* product
* sass
* css
* js

Each section is described below. **None of these have changed shape
in v2.0.0** — an existing gulp-config.js needs no edits.

### browserSync

This section contains the configuration for the "sync" function.  It
has one element, `proxyTarget`, which defines the URL which should be
reloaded when a resource changes.

### gulp

This section defines properties of the project's gulp environment.  It
has one element, `files` which defines an array of glob patterns
matching the files involved in the gulp script of the project.  These
patterns identify the files validated by the `gulpJsLint` task.  A
typical project will have a gulpfile.js and gulp-config.js file in
this list:

```javascript
gulp: { files: ["./gulpfile.js", "./gulp-config.js"] }
```

### product

This section defines methods for identifying the products of the gulp
operations.  It contains these elements:

* dirs -- an array of directory glob patterns that contain build
  products.  These directories are deleted when the `clean` task is
  executed.
  
* files -- an array of glob patterns matching the build products of
  the gulp tasks.  These files are deleted when the `clean` task is
  executed.  These files are also watched by the `watch` operation and
  trigger a browser reload when they change.
  
* checksums -- a directory into which source file checksums are
  written when a build is performed.  These checksums can be used to
  determine if the products are out of date with the sources.  If this
  entry is omitted, no checksums are generated during a build.

### sass

This section defines the sass files that are processed into CSS by a
build.  If this section is omitted, no SASS processing is done.  It
contains these elements:

* sources -- an array of glob patterns matching the SCSS files to be
  processed.

* destination -- the directory path into which the CSS products are
  written.  Directory paths beginning with "." are relative to the
  corresponding SCSS file.

### css

This section describes processing of CSS files, including those
produced from SASS. CSS processing is handled in 2 stages:
concatenation, and minification.  Lists of CSS files to be
concatenated are assembled, then individual CSS files are minified to
a final destination. The elements of the css section are:

* concatenate -- an array of two element objects defining the
  concatenation operation.  If this section is omitted, no
  concatenated products are produced.  The elements are:
  
  * sources -- an array of glob patterns matching the files to
    concatenate together.
  
  * destination -- the file produced by the concatenation.

* sources -- an array of Glob patterns matching the CSS files to be
  minified.  If any of the concatenation products are to be minified,
  they must be matched by a sources pattern.  If this element is
  omitted, no minification is performed.

* exclude -- an optional array of glob patterns matching already
  minified CSS.  If the sources patterns matches existing minified
  files, this pattern can be used to exclude those files to prevent
  unnecessary minification.

* destination -- a directory into which the minified files and
  corresponding map files will be written.  If the path begins with
  "." the path is relative to the directory containing the
  corresponding CSS file.

### js

This section defines parameters for performing operations on
Javascript sources.  These sources are passed both to the lint
operation and to the minifier to generate slimmed down Javascript
files.  It contains the following elements:

* sources - an array of Glob patterns matching the Javascript files to
  be processed.  If this element is omitted, no Javascript processing
  is performed.

* exclude -- an optional array of glob patterns matching already
  minified Javascript.  If the sources patterns matches existing minified
  files, this pattern can be used to exclude those files to prevent
  unnecessary minification.

* destination - a directory in which the minified output are placed.

## Developing gulp-build itself

This repo has its own `gulpfile.js` and `eslint.config.js` at the
root, separate from anything shipped to consumers. They're not part
of the published package — `package.json`'s `files` allowlist
excludes them, along with anything else not explicitly listed there.

They exist to dogfood the package against itself: `npx gulp` (or
`npm test`) runs `gulpJsLint` — the same task consuming projects get
— against this repo's own `index.js`, `gulpfuncs.js`, and
`eslint-config.js`, using `eslint.config.js` here to require the
shared config the package exports. If the shared config can't lint
the package's own source cleanly, it's broken for every consuming
project too, so this is worth running before publishing a new
version.

## Changelog

### 2.0.2

Two more fixes from that same first-project migration, both in
`stylelint-config.json` — this config was carried over from the
original file mostly unmodified and had never actually been run
against real `@use`/`@forward`-based SCSS or the `sass:color` module
until now:

* `at-rule-no-unknown`'s `ignoreAtRules` list had `use` but not
  `forward`, so any `@forward` statement was flagged as an unknown
  at-rule.
* `scss/at-function-named-arguments` was set to `"never"` (forbidding
  named arguments except in single-argument calls). This directly
  conflicts with `sass:color` functions like `color.adjust()`, which
  require naming which channel you're adjusting — there's no
  positional-argument way to call them. Disabled (`null`).

### 2.0.1

Fixes discovered while migrating the first real consuming project
over to 2.0.0: the `.stylelintrc.js`-instead-of-`.stylelintrc.json`
fix (see the callout under step 5), the `stylelint-no-browser-hacks`
removal, the `overrides` for `file-entry-cache`/`immutable`/`postcss`,
the `files` allowlist, and the self-validation `gulpfile.js`/
`eslint.config.js`. Published as a distinct version specifically so
no one's npm cache can confuse it with an earlier, broken fetch of
`2.0.0` — see the version-bump note under "Updating the gulp-build
npm package" below.

### 2.0.0

Modernization pass — see the package's `CHANGELOG.md` for full
details. Highlights relevant to consuming projects:

* **Breaking:** requires Node 22+ (was Gulp 4 on Node 16). A
  `package.json` `engines` field now declares this, so `npm install`
  will warn if it's run on an older Node.
* **Breaking:** ESLint config moved from `.eslintrc.json` to flat
  `eslint.config.js` (ESLint 9). Update projects per step 5 above.
* **Breaking:** the stylelint config must be consumed via a
  `.stylelintrc.js` doing `require('@dltg/gulp-build/stylelint-config')`,
  not a `.stylelintrc.json` with an `"extends"` string — stylelint's
  own resolver for `extends` isn't reliably `exports`-map-aware for
  scoped-package subpaths, and fails with `TypeError: Cannot read
  properties of undefined (reading 'ignoreFiles')`. See the callout
  under step 5 above.
* **Breaking:** the `composerJsonLint` task has been removed.
* JS minification switched from UglifyJS to Terser (`gulp-uglify` →
  `gulp-terser`) — task name (`js`) and behavior are unchanged, just
  the underlying minifier.
* CSS autoprefixing and minification switched from
  `gulp-autoprefixer`/`gulp-clean-css` to a PostCSS pipeline
  (`autoprefixer` + `cssnano` via `gulp-postcss`) — no
  configuration-facing change.
* `clean` now uses `rimraf` instead of `del`.
* New: `@dltg/gulp-build/eslint-config` and
  `@dltg/gulp-build/stylelint-config` subpath exports, replacing the
  old `templates/` copy-or-symlink files.
* Dropped `stylelint-no-browser-hacks`. Its one rule
  (`plugin/no-browser-hacks`) was already disabled (`null`) in the
  shared config, so this has no effect on lint output. It's being
  removed because the plugin bundles its own private copy of
  `stylelint@13` internally rather than running against whichever
  stylelint version is actually installed — a strong sign it hasn't
  been meaningfully maintained since the stylelint 13 era — and it
  was the source of a stale nested `rimraf@3`/`glob@7`/`inflight`
  dependency chain. Note: `stylelint@15` itself pulls a similar old
  chain via `file-entry-cache` → `flat-cache`; that one is out of our
  control until a future stylelint major updates it, and is low-risk
  noise (internal cache-file cleanup only).

  **Update:** actually fixed via an `overrides` entry forcing
  `file-entry-cache` to `^8.0.0`, which uses `flat-cache@4` — a
  release that dropped the `rimraf`/`glob`/`inflight` chain entirely
  in favor of Node's built-in `fs`. This is a real upstream version
  (built and tested together by file-entry-cache's own maintainers),
  not us forcing an incompatible major onto old code, so it's lower
  risk than overriding `rimraf`/`glob` directly would have been.
  Worth a smoke test of both `gulp sass` (stylelint) and `gulp jsLint`
  (ESLint also uses `file-entry-cache` for its own `--cache` option)
  after installing, since the override applies wherever the package
  name appears in the tree, not just under stylelint.
* Two `npm audit` findings fixed via further scoped overrides, both
  transitive and both fixed by version bumps within their existing
  major (not the risky cross-major jumps `npm audit fix --force`
  would have made — it wanted to downgrade `browser-sync` to 1.9.2
  and `gulp-sourcemaps` to 2.6.5, which would have undone most of
  this modernization):
  - `immutable` (via `browser-sync` → `browser-sync-ui`, a dashboard
    feature this package doesn't use) → overridden to `^4.3.9`, the
    very next patch release, which fixes both advisories with no API
    change.
  - `postcss` (via `gulp-sourcemaps` → `@gulp-sourcemaps/identity-map`
    — the same dormant package flagged earlier for `source-map-resolve`)
    → overridden, scoped to just that nested dependency, to `^8.5.23`,
    a security-patch release within the same 8.x line already used
    elsewhere in the tree.
* Dropped several other unmaintained/unused indirect dependencies
  (`lodash`, `through2`, `gulp-fs-cache`, `ansi-colors`, `fancy-log`,
  and a few dependencies that were never actually referenced by any
  task). No task-facing behavior change.
* `package.json` has an `overrides` entry forcing
  `eslint-config-airbnb-base` to accept the ESLint 9 that's actually
  installed. `eslint-config-airbnb-base@15` still declares a peer
  range of `^7.32.0 || ^8.2.0`
  ([airbnb/javascript#2961](https://github.com/airbnb/javascript/issues/2961)
  is tracking their v9 support), which npm's default strict
  peer-resolution will otherwise refuse to install alongside ESLint
  9. In practice the airbnb-base *rules* work fine under ESLint 9 —
  it's only the package's declared peer range that's stale — so
  overriding it is safe. This can be removed once airbnb-base ships
  real ESLint 9 support upstream.

## Updating the gulp-build npm package

To publish an updated version of the gulp-build package:

1. Configure registry access as described above.

2. Update the version number of the package inside the project's
   package.json file. **Always bump it, even for a small fix** — do
   not reuse an existing version number via GitLab's delete-and-rebuild
   option. Beyond GitLab disallowing a duplicate version outright,
   npm's local package cache keys on version + content hash: if a
   broken or stale copy of a given version ever got fetched into
   someone's cache, republishing a fix under that *same* version
   number means their `npm install` can keep silently serving the old
   cached copy — surfacing as confusing failures (e.g. a `.json` file
   that reads as empty or truncated) that have nothing to do with
   what's actually in the registry. A new version number sidesteps
   this categorically; `npm cache clean --force` is the fallback if a
   stale copy is already suspected.

3. Run `npm publish`.

   For a change that alters behavior for consuming projects (a new
   major dependency version, a removed/renamed task, a changed
   config-file format like the v2.0.0 ESLint move), bump the major
   version and update this README's Changelog section. Consuming
   projects should then be upgraded one at a time rather than all at
   once, so a problem in one project doesn't block the rest.
